questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Real-world fault tolerance requires dynamic policy changes without redeploys. This tests design extensibility, runtime registries, and per-endpoint isolation.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime extensibility and registries
- Pipeline/Chain of Responsibility pattern
- Per-endpoint isolation and non-blocking evaluation
- Metrics and safe error handling

## Code Example
```javascript
interface IPolicy { name: string; configure(params: any): void; onCall(ctx: any, next: () => Promise<any>): Promise<any> }
interface IPolicyFactory { create(config?: any): IPolicy }
class PolicyRegistry { private map = new Map<string, IPolicyFactory>(); register(name: string, f: IPolicyFactory): void; create(name: string, config?: any): IPolicy }
class PolicyPipeline { constructor(policies: IPolicy[]); async execute(ctx: any, fn: ()=> Promise<any>): Promise<any> }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test policy interactions across distributed instances?
- How would you handle policy versioning and backward compatibility?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a small, extensible plugin system using runtime registries and the separation of concerns between formatting and sinking.

## Key Concepts
- Registry pattern for dynamic extensibility
- Strategy/Factory for pluggable formatters
- Async I/O and backpressure in sinks
- Graceful shutdown and error containment

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Formatter { format(msg: string, level: string): string; }
interface Sink { write(data: string): Promise<void>; }
class Registry {
  private formats = new Map<string, Formatter>();
  private sinks = new Map<string, Sink>();
  registerFormat(name: string, f: Formatter): void
  getFormat(name: string): Formatter
  registerSink(name: string, s: Sink): void
  getSink(name: string): Sink
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test runtime registration of new formats?
- How would you prevent a slow sink from blocking others?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design extensible, runtime-modifiable tooling using common patterns.

## Key Concepts
- Command pattern, Registry, Factory, dynamic imports, plugin isolation
- Runtime extension without recompilation, error handling, help aggregation

## Code Example
```typescript
// Minimal interfaces
interface Command { execute(args: string[]): Promise<void> }
interface CommandFactory { create(): Command }
class CommandRegistry { register(name: string, factory: () => Command); resolve(name: string): Command; list(): string[] }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you sandbox/unload plugins, handle conflicting command names, and security concerns?
- How would you version plugins and roll back faulty ones?
